Package hadur2.core.shieldmode

Class ShieldBudget

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.shieldmode.ShieldBudget
public final class ShieldBudget extends Object
SHIELD-6: how much bullet damage shield mode may cost over a battle. Once the enemy's bullet damage exceeds what would hold our score share at HOLD_SHARE over the whole battle, shield mode is left for the rest of the battle.

The score share is ours over the pair's total, as the rumble takes it. The core cannot know the final scores, so the budget is worked out from the battle's length and what has happened:

   ours    = 60 * rounds in the battle + damage we dealt so far
   allowed = ours * (1 - HOLD_SHARE) / HOLD_SHARE
   leave shield mode when the enemy's bullet damage > allowed

With the enemy's bullet damage as its whole score, ours/(ours + damage) stays at or above HOLD_SHARE exactly while the damage is within allowed. The 60 is a round's survival bonus (50) and last-survivor bonus (10) in a 1v1, counted for every round of the battle: shield mode is there to win them, so the battle is read as won and the budget asks how much damage that can afford. For a 35-round battle the allowance starts at about 370 (35 * 60 * 15/85), which is DrussGT's limit for the robots on its list, and rises by 0.176 per point of damage we deal. It does not move with rounds won or lost: a round lost shows in the damage taken. Kill bonuses and ramming scores are left out of both sides; ours is a lower bound, so the budget errs towards leaving early.

The round count is the engine's getNumRounds(); when it is not known (0) the rumble's 35 is assumed. Damage counts every enemy bullet that hit us in the battle, in shield mode or out of it. Plain arithmetic, no state beyond two counters.
